summary: Rebuild from the sealed product vision, not the retired source. Preserve full safety and truth requirements while reducing generation amplification through a compact ownership architecture, frozen cross-module interfaces, behavior-grouped tests, and an explicit Provider-call stop condition.
diagnosis: The product scope is legitimate but the previous fresh plan fragmented Backend and Tests into nineteen leaves each, multiplying interface drift, prompt context, retries, and Provider exposure.
The durable value is the Demo acquisition, parser proof, conservative analysis contract, and report truth; the retired module layout is not authoritative and must not be copied.

High-risk boundaries are input provenance and extraction safety, parser normalization, information-state uncertainty, and conclusion wording. These must be frozen as interfaces before source generation.
A real unlabeled Demo can prove execution and signal coverage only. It cannot establish classification accuracy or authorize automatic action.
provider_guidance: Use one compact dependency-ordered architecture: contracts/models; reviewed catalog plus bounded transport/acquisition; parser normalization; geometry plus analysis; report; workflow plus CLI. Keep public interfaces explicit and avoid generic stage frameworks.

Freeze typed payloads first: SourceManifest, ParserProof, NormalizedDemo, InformationState, SignalWindow, PlayerAssessment, AnalysisReport, and stable error codes. Every downstream file must import these contracts instead of redefining shapes.

Generate implementation in ownership groups and validate each group before continuing: input safety, parser, analysis, reporting/CLI. Do not begin Tests until those public interfaces pass syntax, import, and interface checks.

Group tests by behavior rather than by symbol: acquisition security; parser proof; geometry/analysis; unknown-information and conclusion truth; CLI/report integration; optional live catalog. Do not split small suites into executable anchor/part trees.

Treat the project as a bounded hybrid rebuild. Stop rather than retry indefinitely when the monitored Provider-request count reaches 24; record NEEDS_REWORK if no candidate exists. Never relax safety, truth, or delivery gates to fit the budget.

For the first acceptance run, analyze the preserved authorized cached Demo without network. Online discovery remains required and tested through contracts, but a new 268 MB download is unnecessary unless cache verification fails.
acceptance_checks: Fresh output and run directories are absent before generation, and no retired source path is present in generated-source provenance or imports.
Generated compile, imports, and substantive tests pass with security, parser, analysis, truth, CLI, and report coverage.
A preserved authorized real Demo completes local parse-to-report with synthetic fallback disabled and non-zero ticks, players, positions, view angles, and available event counts.

Independent assertions prove unknown information remains unknown, unsupported hidden-information signals are disabled, accuracy is NOT_EVALUATED, automatic bans are false, and human review is required.
Only the reviewed route may materialize source; only local_packager may create a delivery bundle after all formal gates pass.
tool_evidence_requests: Monitor provider_phase_log.jsonl and terminate the bounded rebuild at 24 Provider requests if it has not completed.
Run generated pytest with PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 and bind the result to the generated source hash.
Run one cached-real-Demo CLI acceptance and independently inspect the emitted JSON report before any packaging decision.
known_limits: A 24-request ceiling is an experimental cost bound, not a proven optimal budget for this large project.
This advisory brief does not generate, edit, package, deliver, or formally pass the new candidate.
